big-agnes-copper-spur-hv-ul2: Roomy freestanding two-person used for years, but zippers fail and wide pads fit tightly.
big-agnes-copper-spur-ul1: Easy freestanding pitch and generous storage; one finds it cramped for a quilt.
big-agnes-copper-spur-ul2: Roomy even for tall hikers, though some report condensation and a floor that wet out in rain.
big-agnes-fly-creek-ul2: Light and long-lasting, often for a decade; tight for two, with limited headroom.
big-agnes-rapide-sl-insulated: Raised rails suit side sleepers, but a good number find it colder than rated and some report leaks.
big-agnes-tiger-wall-ul1: Light, easy-pitching solo tent that survives hard use and wind; suits smaller hikers best.
big-agnes-tiger-wall-ul2: Very roomy for one and used on long thru-hikes, but zippers snag and the fabric can tear.
durston-kakwa-40: Light frame moves weight to the hips and the inside is roomy; some find the bottle pockets small.
durston-kakwa-55: Carries heavy loads well while staying light; some can't get a fit and a sweaty back is common.
durston-wapta-30: Comfortable for a frameless pack, but the shoulder straps hurt some as loads rise.
durston-x-dome-1: Roomy, freestanding and solid in weather, though not the lightest and a few report pole trouble.
durston-x-dome-2: Roomy with an easy freestanding pitch; the main gripe is bent poles in gusts and torn floors.
durston-x-mid-1: Generous vestibules and storm performance; the big footprint leaves a snug bed for taller hikers.
durston-x-mid-1-solid: Warm and wind-proof for the weight; the solid inner is stuffy in heat and sags on uneven ground.
durston-x-mid-2: Often a palace for one and roomy for two, but the large footprint is hard to fit on uneven sites.
durston-x-mid-2-solid: Copes well with storms and cold; large footprint, tricky on uneven ground and stuffy when humid.
durston-x-mid-pro-1: Headroom and a low zippered storm pitch, but uneven ground is fussy and condensation shows up.
durston-x-mid-pro-2: Light and storm-worthy with a quick pitch; the footprint is hard to place and the floor seems frail.
durston-x-mid-pro-2-plus: Space for two, a dog and gear at low weight; needs a large flat site, and a few had floor damage.
enlightened-equipment-enigma: Light and packable, but a sizable group find it colder than rated, with drafts and shifting down.
enlightened-equipment-revelation: Light and versatile, but nearly as many find it colder than rated, with drafts and down shifting.
gossamer-gear-kumo-36: Surprisingly comfortable for a frameless pack at a fair price; a couple report the pockets tearing.
gossamer-gear-mariposa-60: Light with roomy pockets and a fair price; the thin fabric tears and the hip belt slips under load.
gossamer-gear-the-one: Quick pitch and room for the weight; condensation is the main gripe, and it runs small for the tall.
gossamer-gear-thinlight-foam-pad: Useful under an inflatable pad against punctures and sliding, though too thin on its own for some.
hyperlite-mountain-gear-20-degree-quilt: Warm near freezing and roomy for side and restless sleepers; a couple call it pricey.
hyperlite-mountain-gear-southwest: Tough and water resistant at moderate loads; the main gripe is shoulder pain past about 25 to 30 lb.
jetboil-minimo-cooking-system: Boils fast and simmers well enough for real cooking, not just hot water.
katabatic-gear-alsek-22-f-quilt: Properly warm around and below freezing with a pad attachment that works; cold sleepers were chilly.
katabatic-gear-flex-15-f-quilt: Comfortable well below freezing, though a few cold sleepers were cold and a couple blamed drafts.
katabatic-gear-flex-22-f-quilt: Comfortable into the teens with layers, and the footbox vents warm nights; drafts are the gripe.
katabatic-gear-flex-30-f-quilt: Pad attachment many call the best around; needs a warm pad, and a few found it too much for summer.
katabatic-gear-palisade-30-f-quilt: Warmer than its rating suggests, with few drafts; a few dislike the narrow cut and fiddly straps.
katabatic-gear-sawatch-15-f-quilt: Genuinely warm even for many cold sleepers, with few drafts; can be too warm in summer.
msr-pocketrocket-2: Tough, compact and reliable for years, though weak in wind and cold and slow to boil.
msr-pocketrocket-deluxe: Fast-boiling, simmers well and handles wind; the piezo igniter failed early for several owners.
nemo-hornet-elite-osmo: Light, durable and storm-worthy; several name the OSMO versions their favourite Hornet so far.
nemo-hornet-osmo: Roomy for its weight and dry in rain, though the 1P is tiny and a few worry it feels delicate.
nemo-switchback: Foam with no leak risk, softer than similar folding pads; bulky, and firm for some side sleepers.
nemo-tensor-all-season: Warm enough for cold nights while staying light and packing small; a few find it noisy or leaky.
nemo-tensor-elite: Packs very small and light yet comfortable; slippery, poor in cool weather and puncture-prone.
nemo-tensor-extreme-conditions: Warm and comfortable on snow and in the cold; complaints are rare, though one pad failed in days.
osprey-exos-48: Excellent back airflow and a build that lasts years; the hip pockets are small and awkward.
osprey-exos-58: Mesh back keeps sweat down and fits a bear canister; comfort fades for some past roughly 30 pounds.
platypus-gravityworks: Filters lots of water fast while hanging, good for groups; clogs or slows after storage.
platypus-quickdraw: Fast flow, an integrity check and caps on both ends; quality control is the worry, with some duds.
sawyer-squeeze: Long-lived and trusted, easy to backflush; slows or clogs after storage and some never fully fix it.
sea-to-summit-ether-light-xr: Very comfortable for side sleepers and packs small; some find it noisy and a bit heavy.
sea-to-summit-spark-pro: Open footbox and zips let hikers vent on mild nights, and several slept warm when it turned cold.
six-moon-designs-gatewood-cape: Very light shelter that doubles as a poncho; condensation and wind are weak, and small for the tall.
six-moon-designs-lunar-solo: Roomy, light and good value, though condensation builds where walls sag and the pitch must be exact.
soto-amicus: Compact, sturdy and good value with stable pot supports; a few say the built-in igniter failed.
soto-windmaster: Efficient, light and strong in wind; the piezo igniter can fail when wet, so many carry a lighter.
tarptent-aeon-li: Very light solo tent with a small footprint, good in wind; snug for the tall and awkward to pack.
tarptent-double-rainbow-li: Generous room for tall hikers; condensation is the main complaint, though several see little.
therm-a-rest-neoair-xlite-nxt: Warm for the weight, but some find it narrow or slippery and several report leaks or valve trouble.
therm-a-rest-neoair-xtherm-nxt: Very warm for its weight, even on snow; several side sleepers got hip pressure or rolled off.
therm-a-rest-z-lite-sol: Tough foam pad that cannot be punctured; firm enough that side sleepers often get sore hips.
toaks-titanium-750ml-pot: A small stove and canister usually nest inside; a few note it's narrow and heats unevenly.
ula-circuit: Very durable, with room for a bear canister; comfort fades once loads pass roughly 30 to 35 lb.
western-mountaineering-alpinlite: Accurate rating and generous cut for side sleepers and layering, though heavy next to quilts.
western-mountaineering-astralite-top-qui: Warm for its weight and well made; the cut is a bit narrow and drafty at the shoulders.
western-mountaineering-megalite: Roomy wider cut and long life, with cautious ratings; one finds it comfortable only near freezing.
western-mountaineering-summerlite: Light, small and durable; several say it feels like a 40F bag, so cold sleepers may want more.
western-mountaineering-terralite: Roomy and warm for restless side sleepers and long lasting; heavy, and one 25 felt cold in the 30s.
western-mountaineering-ultralite: Very warm for its weight, used into the teens by many; the snug cut and shallow hood bothered some.
western-mountaineering-versalite: Cold sleepers especially love it and some last many years; a few found it overkill or bulky.
zpacks-arc-haul-ultra: Comfortable and ventilated under heavy loads; some report worn stays, tears and bad stitching.
